items.method: Cross-read the options-flow lean (call-versus-put premium and the top same-session prints) against the options-structure corridor (negative dealer gamma, flip, put and call walls, expected move), then test that bullish-flow signal against equity internals — the defensive sector rotation out of financials and market-heatmap breadth — to judge whether aggressive call buying is being ratified or resisted, and anchor invalidation to the put-wall level the corridor mechanically depends on.
items.note: The genuinely new signature this window is an aggressive bullish options tape landing on top of a mechanically pinned, defensively-rotating equity market. Option premium has flipped from balanced to firmly call-heavy — $1.606B of call premium against $854.5M of put premium at a 0.6527 call fraction across 12 tickers, 1483 contracts clearing the $250k bar inside 30 days — and the single heaviest print is an SPY 764 call at $33.7M on 339.8x its open interest, a same-session index-upside bet stacked right at spot. Yet the structure model puts SPY in negative dealer gamma with spot near 764.1 sitting directly on the 764 put wall, only about 5 points under the 769.14 flip, inside a plus-or-minus 2.86 expected move, while the sector model is rotating defensively into staples (XLP, Leading, accel +4.01) and specifically out of financials (XLF, Weakening) and market-heatmap breadth is still only 58.1% of 134 constituents, 1.9 points shy of the 60% broad-participation line. So call buyers are pressing upside into a corridor that dealers must sell into and that equity leadership and breadth have not confirmed. Watch a reclaim of the 769.14 flip and breadth clearing the 60% line as the confirming triggers; because this is a constructive, upside-pressing read, it is invalidated on a daily close below ~764.00 on SPY, which loses the 764 put wall in negative gamma and reopens downside toward the lower strikes.

items.method: Cross-read the sector-rotation RRG state for financials (XLF relative-momentum quadrant and acceleration), the causal-rotation candidate on banks (stage, plan-eligibility, confirmation-versus-contradiction count) and the bond model's high-yield-versus-investment-grade price-pulse direction to locate where the three models agree and disagree on the credit-and-banks node, then place that against the defensive equity rotation and anchor the constructive index-level read's invalidation to the SPY put wall the corridor depends on.
items.note: The new convergence this window is that three independent models are all pointing at banks and credit at once, and they disagree on sign. The sector model is rotating specifically out of financials — XLF reads Weakening with one-month relative momentum -0.32 even as its three- and six-month relative momentum stays positive — while staples (XLP) accelerate into Leading. The causal model's top candidate is selective credit transmission into banks (exposure exp:banks) held at a watch stage: not plan-eligible, one independent confirmation against one contradiction, confirmation still required. And the bond model reads the high-yield-versus-investment-grade price ratio strengthening across both aligned pairs (jnk-lqd, hyg-lqd) through 2026-08-21 while withholding a directional credit call for lack of an independent credit-spread reading. So the credit-and-banks complex is the genuinely contested node: relative-price and causal work lean constructive-but-unconfirmed on credit selectivity, while the equity rotation is actively leaving financials. This read is constructive on the credit/risk side and is expressed at the index level, so watch XLF reclaiming a Leading state and the causal candidate advancing past watch with breadth clearing 60% as the confirming triggers; it is invalidated on a daily close below ~764.00 on SPY, which breaks the put-wall support the constructive index read leans on.
